rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports on grave visitation establish its legitimacy, wisdom, timing, method, and etiquette.

rows.speaker: author

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Visitors may recite Qur'an and dedicate its reward, while seeking Allah's will and preparing in complete faith for their own death.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The visit should prompt reflection on resurrection, judgment, the scales, and the destinations of deeds, strengthening resolve for faith and righteous action over rivalry and accumulation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dead have returned or been returned to Allah and enter their final states according to their standing before Him.
rows.anchor: Ölenler, indallah mertebelerine göre ya îşe-i râzıyeye

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prophetic report says a person will be resurrected with those he loves, so those who love the good join the good and those who love evil join the evil.
rows.anchor: اَلْمَرْءُ مَعَ مَنْ أَحَبَّ sevdikleriyle haşrolunacaklarından iyileri sevenler iyilerle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Love is valuable when it is for Allah and follows the command to follow the Prophet.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dead have passed on: their deeds are theirs and yours are yours, so boasting or competing over them has no point.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship and seeking aid belong to Allah; helping people for Allah is praised, while begging people is blameworthy, and asking the dead is especially unfitting.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One benefits from the deceased by reflecting on their lives and works and keeping their good example alive.

rows.speaker: İbn Âbidîn

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A grave visit can affect a person like reading a book, awakening memories and reflection.

rows.speaker: author

rows.speaker: author

rows.speaker: author

rows.speaker: author

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath encompasses every meaning of asr, especially the final era as the afternoon of time and the age of Muhammad, before the declaration that humankind is in loss.
rows.anchor: Her mânasıyla asra ve bâhusus pek büyük hâdisâta

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The generic al-insan, signaled by the following exception, means all humanity across eras, especially people of the last era, are in absolute loss except those named next.
rows.anchor: insan lâm, istisnâ karînesiyle istiğrak içindir, yani her insan bütün nev‘-i beşer her asırda

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Husr means losing rather than gaining, wasting capital, and ending in bankruptcy, sorrow, and deprivation; the indefinite form magnifies or specifies the kind of loss.
rows.anchor: “Hüsr” ü “hüsran”, kazanacak yerde ziyan etmek, sermayeyi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Life is humanity's capital: it is spent with every breath and hour, while accountability for this blessing approaches.
rows.anchor: Çünkü insanın sermayesi ömrüdür, o ise her nefes, her saat

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Life is a limited loan belonging to the Creator, entrusted to people to invest well; their benefit depends on the profit made by spending it.
rows.anchor: insanın kendi milki değil, yaratan Hâlık teâlâ’nın milki olup O’nun nâmına güzel tasarruf ederek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person receives only what they strive for and is held accountable for what they earn.
rows.anchor: İnsanın bütün istifadesi onun sarf u mübâdelesinden hâsıl olacak kâra bağlıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After returning the loaned capital to its owner, people are saved and rewarded according to their profit or left liable, bankrupt, and punished according to their deficit; the scales express this reckoning.
rows.anchor: hesap günü kendisine kalacak olan kâra göre kendisini kurtaracak ve o nisbette mütena‘‘im olacak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every breath spent idly is loss; a worldly or neutral act leaves no lasting gain, evil is certainly loss, and even obedience could have been done better.
rows.anchor: Bir mubah ise bir eseri kalmamak itibariyle boşuna geçmiş gibidir. Bir şer ise muhakkak bir hüsrandır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because knowledge of Allah and His majesty can grow without limit, greater knowledge should produce deeper awe and love and more complete worship; settling for less entails some loss.
rows.anchor: insanın Allah’a ilmi ne kadar çok olursa haşyet ve mahabbeti de o nisbette çok

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obstacles and constricting events that assail people compound the danger and loss inherent in the passing of time.
rows.anchor: asrın, zamanın cereyânı içinde her taraftan hücum etmekte bulunan mâni‘aları

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if people enjoyed constant comfort, their lives move toward death and each passing breath is itself a death.
rows.anchor: her dem ömrü ölüme doğru gitmekte bulunan insanın bir hüsran içinde bulunduğunu inkâr etmek kābil olmaz

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Razi says loss is humanity's basic condition: true happiness is loving the afterlife rather than attaching oneself to worldly pain and pleasure, yet most people pursue the world and are ruined.
rows.anchor: Bundan dolayı Râzî der ki: “Bu âyet insanda hüsran ve haybetin asl

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those with the four traits named in the next verse are exceptions to loss and instead gain.
rows.anchor: Ancak o kimseler müstesnâ şu zikrolunacak dört vasıf ile muttasıf olanlar hüsranda değil, kârdadırlar
